distribution_boundary.description: Owner decisions of 19 November 2026. Distributed: the source code in the public OpenMettle repositories that are not forks, and the Helm chart in openmettle-deploy. Explicit exception: OpenMettle/openmettle-serving, a public non-fork repository of experimental ROCm/SGLang serving and benchmarking work, stays outside the boundary until serving packaging (V1-20) audits the serving stack, the same treatment as the SGLang fork. OpenMettle/openmettle-acp, a public non-fork repository with its own LICENSE and NOTICE, is inside the boundary. This register's gate covers openmettle-core's own source only; every other in-boundary repository is reviewed in its own repository. Not distributed yet: built container images (including the core api, worker and migrate images), re-hosted third-party images, curated forks and model weights. The public forks OpenMettle/sglang and OpenMettle/open-webui stay outside the boundary as public forks under their upstream licences: the SGLang fork comes inside, with a full audit, when serving packaging (V1-20) ships it; the Open WebUI fork is reference material for the product OpenMettle replaces and stays public. Third-party images are referenced only at their publishers' locations. Long-term direction: distribute everything needed to run OpenMettle, eventually as an Arch Linux distribution with everything preinstalled except components whose licences do not allow redistribution. Each widening of the boundary is a separate owner decision; publishing the core images (V1-36) is the likely next one.

review.notes: Recorded by an agent from the owner's decision comments. The third supersedes the second's fork item: both public forks stay outside the boundary for now. The fourth names openmettle-serving as an explicit exception, places openmettle-acp inside the boundary with its licence review in its own repository, and limits this register's gate to openmettle-core's own source. It defines distribution scope only; it is not a licence review or legal clearance.

review.notes: Proposed by an agent on 19 November 2026 and approved by the owner the same day, with CC0-1.0 dropped and MIT-0 added; an agent transcribed the approval from the owner's decision comment. Approval adopts a licence-bookkeeping policy; packages are reviewed against policy, which is not legal clearance.
